invariants.statement: A successful foundational mutation closes only with committed audit evidence or an explicit durable audit-deferred state that remains reconciliation-required.
invariants.title: Audit closure precedes successful outcome

invariants.statement: The installed adapter accepts exactly one bounded closed-shape JSON command on standard input and emits exactly one bounded JSON result on standard output.
invariants.title: Bounded one-value process framing

invariants.statement: Recovery advances only from exact predecessor, active-attempt, and re-observed state evidence and never from time, recency, or process age.
invariants.title: Evidence-driven forward recovery

invariants.statement: Invocation and description bind the exact immutable receipt-v2 executable, entry point, digests, protocol, and compatible capability set without newest-version selection.
invariants.title: Exact adapter provenance

invariants.statement: A mutation is permitted only for an unexpired immutable plan bound to the exact observed state and exact expected durable attempt state, with the attempt committed before host mutation.
invariants.title: Plan and attempt compare-and-swap

invariants.statement: Human CLI and machine adapter entry points delegate to the same module-owned transaction engine and expose no bypass around expected-state, attempt, purge-safety, audit, or recovery rules.
invariants.title: Shared module transaction core

invariants.statement: Stable state identity includes all mutation-relevant and recovery evidence while excluding documentary observation time; the full observation digest binds both.
invariants.title: Stable observation digests

invariants.statement: Every new installable module or administrator-facing interaction declares a stable feature identity and reviewed qxctl and backend mapping or an explicit evidence-backed disposition in the same admission change; omission remains uncovered.
invariants.title: Module administration declaration

invariants.statement: Every executable qxctl Cobra leaf has one stable qxcmd identity and exact reviewed grammar, feature and interaction binding, backend-operation binding, mutability, authority, target-scope, noninteractive, structured-result, and recovery metadata; the checked-in expected registry is byte-semantically equal to the executable command tree.
invariants.title: qxctl command registry parity

invariants.statement: The qxctl evidence workflow pins caller intent, exact owner installations, corpus selections and native artifact provenance before advancing durable stages. Immutable content and validation records have separate digests. Status preserves its stated integrity scope; recovery reconstructs stage inputs and replays exact owner results, rejecting changed inputs, missing evidence and substituted checkpoints. Runs create no selected head, provider facts or permission. The four additive .6 pack/composition artifact kinds retain their original exact operation, authored input, result and owner installation; generated interface admission neither promotes metadata listing into native replay nor substitutes a current owner for historical provenance. The additive .7 composition workflow binds its root/TOPS, selected composition owner and exact caller request; package stages execute through each retained pack original owner. Every checkpoint must match the requested stage and reconstructed input. Typed journal roundtrip rejects field omission or null normalization under an old digest. Progress and conformance remain separate; failed fixtures and native evidence/implementation obligations survive a completed workflow. Exact obligation links bind original composition records, the follow-up owner record, root/TOPS and submitted provenance identity. Retention publishes the native result before its immutable link; exact retries reuse records. Show replays original owners and rejects substituted linkage rather than adopting current caller installation. A bounded exact record envelope accounts for its independently bounded input and native result; other objects and each child retain their original value and byte limits.
invariants.title: Agent workflow recovery preserves exact caller intent and native evidence

invariants.statement: The corpus owner validates sealed indexes, exact domain scope, member identity against the supplied immediate predecessor and consistent latest/retained-complete evidence. Query preserves source revision and observation age; removed selection is not retirement. Capture-index metadata alone cannot prove backing bytes, and no pure result selects a durable head or grants authority.
invariants.title: Corpus projections preserve exact indexed evidence and selected coverage

invariants.statement: The local corpus adapter binds original operation inputs and installation before work, checkpoints exact completed capture/index pairs, publishes immutable objects without replacement and exposes a snapshot only after referenced evidence is durable and verified within declared bounds. Recovery retains exact source inputs and completed results; clock rollback cannot freeze an invalid snapshot. No selected corpus head, latest alias or SSIAG/STAV authority is created by job bookkeeping.
invariants.title: Immutable corpus retention exposes only reconstructable exact snapshots

invariants.statement: The protected graph-selection adapter retains an exact engine-validated graph and installation in durable intent before authorization, compares both the expected graph digest and selection generation under serialization, and exposes only one coherent committed head with contiguous publication history. A prepared or interrupted attempt cannot become a selected graph without current validated authority.
invariants.title: Protected graph selection commits only exact validated and authorized evidence

invariants.statement: The C++ interpretation owner validates exact sealed profiles and capture bindings, retains qualified extraction findings and replays wrapped interpretations before evaluating caller-defined subject/scope/type/unit checks. Reassessment replays both retained results and distinguishes changed inputs and affected findings. Missing, stale, disputed or conditional support cannot become unqualified runtime compatibility, provider-wide contradiction or authority. Recomputed outer digests do not bypass nested replay. Native profile preparation validates and seals exactly the authored draft without asserting source extraction or substituting fields. Portable provider packs preserve caller-authored declarations, exact profile and fixture expectations, detached-input identity, structured token provenance and explicit failed/unrun conformance. Finite recipe exploration and reassessment reconstruct selected evidence, requirements, allowed choices, enumeration bounds, interface declarations and obligations without ranking providers, silently relaxing requirements, or treating authored implementation metadata as observed compatibility. Native obligation inventory binds each precise check or other work subject to the full replayed composition. Follow-up replays both sides, preserves all non-time caller criteria and policy, reports query-time differences, and never credits an opaque reference with proof or causation. Non-check obligations remain separately unverified.
invariants.title: Profile and connection results preserve replayable scoped evidence

invariants.statement: The C++ coverage owner replays the declared provider candidate, exact corpus query and independent interpretation wrappers before accounting for inventory, selection and authored rule attempts. Missing or unlisted sources, unselected or stale captures, partial acquisition, declaration drift and unresolved extraction remain explicit. Metadata alone cannot prove body availability, matched rules cannot become runtime support, and recomputed outer seals cannot conceal changed joins or counts. The qxctl consumer independently rejects substituted inventories, source/capture bindings and summaries.
invariants.title: Provider coverage preserves declared scope and exact selected evidence

invariants.statement: Source reducers reject stale or altered expected-state transitions; capture and graph consumers revalidate retained bytes, domain qualification and semantic digests. A computed transition or projection is evidence and cannot assert authorization or a durable storage commit. Mechanical interface generation preserves exact earlier release admissions; receipt-owned declaration inspection binds retained bytes and canonical metadata to the compiled owner interface. Generated metadata does not replace independent semantic validation or admit arbitrary executable behavior.
invariants.title: Source-knowledge process preserves exact domain evidence and revision lineage

invariants.statement: The source storage adapter serializes expected-state comparison, retains the exact C++ plan/transition and installation as durable intent before requesting trusted audited SSIAG authorization, and commits only that authorized successor. Recovery observes original operation identity and actual head; denial or an interrupted attempt cannot claim successful mutation.
invariants.title: Protected source mutation binds exact owner transition before durable commit

invariants.statement: SSIAG provider binding inventory and mutation use only exact receipt-bound installation identities; no timestamp, filesystem order, or newest version selects a binding. Apply re-verifies candidate evidence, commits distinct safe STAV evidence before state mutation, advances durable attempts only through prepared, candidate_verified, audited, and committed, and uses exact compare-and-swap so recovery can move forward or backward only along one uniquely evidenced plan. The attempt preserves the initiating safe audit identity so a newly authorized recovery caller can reconstruct the original idempotent STAV candidate without inheriting the initiating caller's authority. The narrow offline recovery lane uses the same manager and requires an exact receipt-v2 foundation, enrolled service identity and target-host ownership, absent live service, and normal STAV closure without enabling provider operations or secret delivery.
invariants.title: Provider binding is exact, audited, and recoverable

invariants.statement: Provider metadata and control framing carries only bounded safe references, operation metadata, descriptor truth, and safe reason codes. Secret bytes, proofs, provider payloads, and secret-shaped diagnostics never enter JSON control, standard output, standard error, arguments, environment variables, qxctl, STAV, or general diagnostics; the trust-only metadata slice creates no secret-bearing channel and keeps operational access disabled.
invariants.title: Provider control and secret channels do not interfere

invariants.statement: Before any provider response is accepted, SSIAG selects one exact receipt-v2 entry point and verifies its allowlisted path, regular-file identity, ownership, mode, bytes, platform, protocol, version, and metadata capability; the adapter independently verifies the invoking SSIAG executable under the ratified path, ownership, receipt, and signing policy. Drift, ambiguity, replacement, incompatibility, or failed mutual trust reports unavailable without fallback or operational access.
invariants.title: Provider executables have mutual exact provenance

invariants.statement: SSIAG readiness preserves three independent layers: native structural signature observation, protected installation-policy requirement evaluation, and an explicitly disabled Phase 10B operational-eligibility gate. Receipt v2 owns every bounded app-bundle file, the cgo-free foundation reconstructs and re-verifies the complete bundle in private staging, and qxctl receives only safe metadata with every operational flag false.
invariants.title: Provider readiness evidence cannot become operational authority
